# Ensuring freedom, one blob at a time — Free Software Foundation — Working together for free software

## Ensuring freedom, one blob at a time

The Free Software Foundation (FSF) was founded to support the work of the [GNU Project](https://www.gnu.org/), and this is still proudly one of our core responsibilities. The GNU Project has delivered some of the most important software used globally, and it is [free as in freedom](https://www.gnu.org/philosophy/free-sw.html). It is a symbol and source of inspiration for those of us who advocate for software freedom. It has been part of the long-lived success of the FSF and the free software philosophy that when we present our convictions, we are able to point to pragmatic implementations of the issues we advocate for. The FSF has a long history of taking action and delivering the software we want to see. This is still true today, and we will not stop.

At the end of 2025, the FSF launched [LibrePhone](https://librephone.fsf.org/), a project that works on closing the last gaps towards free [mobile phone computing](https://librephone.fsf.org/freedom). LibrePhone's goal is to better understand and reverse-engineer the [nonfree blobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binary_blob) used by a great majority of (if not all) SoCs (system on a chip) designs available today. We started with [researching](https://librephone.fsf.org/site/files/) the proprietary files in Android phones supported by the [Lineage](https://wiki.lineageos.org/) project, an Android-based volunteer-led mobile phone operating system with much free software already in it. Our current, primary focus is on the radio blobs that control WiFi, Bluetooth, NFC, and cellular communications. The software freedom issues with [mobile computing](https://www.fsf.org/working-together/next-steps/free-software-phones) have been around for a long time, with the most challenging issue being the baseband/modem firmware that relies heavily on proprietary software. This creates a technical and legal maze that is nearly impossible to break free from, but that doesn't mean we should ever stop working to create free systems. It certainly doesn't mean we shouldn't liberate the software that we know *can* be free software.

Now, half a year into this project, lead developer Rob Savoye has extracted firmware from over 200 Lineage install packages, processed 85GB of files, and imported the results of these analyses into a [PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/) database for [cross-device comparison. By focusing on [one device](https://librephone.fsf.org/hardware/fairphone6), we envisioned we would have the best opportunity to work towards a truly libre phone that could serve as an example. This was done to get a feel for which blobs are the most common, identify the best blobs for reverse engineering, and select the best initial development device for [reverse engineering](https://librephone.fsf.org/site/tools/). We [found](https://librephone.fsf.org/site/comparing/) instead, among other things, that much of the software and blobs we need to work through are shared across multiple devices; this means even greater strides for mobile phone freedom.

Freeing even just one aspect of mobile phone computing is a huge task, and the work on LibrePhone will take a long time, but so was creating a fully free OS in [1983](https://www.gnu.org/). Look where we are forty years after the FSF's founding! Sometimes it feels like so much is bending towards the will of power and finance in technology that it can be hard to think positively about the future of software freedom. We get buried every day in news about the threats to copylefted software by [large language models](https://www.fsf.org/news/fsf-is-working-on-freedom-in-machine-learning-applications), increased [vendor lock-ins](https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026/04/fcc-says-ban-on-foreign-made-routers-includes-portable-wi-fi-hotspots/), and so-called "[cloud](https://www.gnu.org/philosophy/who-does-that-server-really-serve.html)" computing. We never stop finding new [license violations](https://www.fsf.org/blogs/licensing/2026-anthropic-settlement) or absurd [privacy violations](https://www.fsf.org/blogs/community/2026-ring-offers-mass-surveillance), and the [rights related to ownership](https://www.fsf.org/blogs/community/your-digital-life-is-not-yours) and [repair of our technology](https://www.fsf.org/campaigns/fight-to-repair) are in need of stronger lines of defense. The FSF is working hard on all those aspects threatening our digital rights, but in the meantime, we are putting our money where our mouth is, and continuing to develop software for freedom. As insurmountable as it may seem at times, every blob we manage to free up will be progress. The FSF has proven t...

In 2026, free software runs [two-thirds](https://www.networkworld.com/article/964836/linux-then-and-why-you-should-learn-it-now.html) of the servers powering the internet, it has 100% market share of the top [500 supercomputers](https://www.zdnet.com/article/all-500-of-the-worlds-fastest-supercomputers-now-run-linux-exclusive/), and [98% of all codebases](https://ia801906.us.archive.org/7/items/rep-ossra-2021/rep-ossra-2021.pdf) contain free software. Tens of millions of individuals also run free software on their personal devices, and many millions more could. Consider all this success, all these enormous accomplishments of free software powering the world's technology, and you'll find that the four freedoms we advocate for — to run, modify, copy, and share software — already have a place in our daily lives. The possibilities of what we can do together are often wildly underestimated or stymied by those who fear them.

Much like with the start of the GNU Project in 1983, we have set out on a journey that we know is a massive undertaking, but given much of our computing is done on mobile phones these days, it is a necessary project. All we need is time, [financial support](https://my.fsf.org/donate?mtm_campaign=summer26&mtm_source=bulletinm) to keep going, [volunteers](https://www.fsf.org/volunteer?mtm_campaign=summer26&mtm_source=bulletinm), and our free software spirit. Let's take matters into our own hands and secure freedom, one blob at a time.

*"[Generic mobile phone in FSF red](https://static.fsf.org/nosvn/bulletin/2026/summer/generic-mobile-phone-in-fsf-red.png)" © 2026, Free Software Foundation, Inc., by Eko Owen. This image is licensed under a [Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) license.*

#### Document Actions

- **[Share on social networks](https://www.fsf.org/share?u=https://www.fsf.org/bulletin/2026/summer/ensuring-freedom-one-blob-at-a-time&t=Ensuring freedom, one blob at a time)**
- [News](https://www.fsf.org/static/fsforg/rss/news.xml)
- [Events](https://www.fsf.org/static/fsforg/rss/events.xml)
- [Blogs](https://www.fsf.org/static/fsforg/rss/blogs.xml)
- [Jobs](https://www.fsf.org/static/fsforg/rss/jobs.xml)
- [GNU](http://www.gnu.org/rss/whatsnew.rss)

# 一個 blob 一個 blob 地守護自由 — 自由軟體基金會 — 攜手推動自由軟體

## 一個 blob 一個 blob 地守護自由

自由軟體基金會（Free Software Foundation, FSF）創立之初，是為了支持 [GNU 專案](https://www.gnu.org/)的工作，而這至今仍是我們引以為傲的核心職責之一。GNU 專案已經交付了若干全球使用的最重要軟體，而且它是[自由意義上的 free](https://www.gnu.org/philosophy/free-sw.html)。對我們這些倡議軟體自由的人而言，它是一個象徵，也是靈感來源。FSF 與自由軟體理念之所以能長久成功，部分原因在於：當我們提出自己的信念時，也能指向我們所倡議議題的務實實作。FSF 長久以來都採取行動，交付我們希望看見的軟體。直到今天仍是如此，而我們不會停下腳步。

2025 年底，FSF 啟動了 [LibrePhone](https://librephone.fsf.org/)；這個專案致力於補上通往自由[手機運算](https://librephone.fsf.org/freedom)的最後缺口。LibrePhone 的目標，是更深入理解並逆向工程現今絕大多數（若非全部）SoC（system on a chip，系統單晶片）設計所使用的[非自由 blob](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binary_blob)。我們一開始先[研究](https://librephone.fsf.org/site/files/) [Lineage](https://wiki.lineageos.org/) 專案所支援 Android 手機中的專有檔案；Lineage 是一個以 Android 為基礎、由志工主導的手機作業系統，其中已經包含許多自由軟體。我們目前的主要重點，是控制 WiFi、藍牙、NFC 與行動通訊的無線電 blob。[行動運算](https://www.fsf.org/working-together/next-steps/free-software-phones)上的軟體自由問題已存在很久，其中最棘手的是基頻／數據機韌體高度依賴專有軟體。這形成了一座幾乎不可能脫身的技術與法律迷宮，但這並不表示我們應該停止打造自由系統；也絕不表示我們不該解放那些我們知道*能夠*成為自由軟體的軟體。

這項計畫進行半年後，首席開發者 Rob Savoye 已經從超過 200 個 Lineage 安裝套件中擷取韌體，處理了 85GB 的檔案，並將這些分析結果匯入 [PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/) 資料庫，用於跨裝置比較。透過聚焦於[一款裝置](https://librephone.fsf.org/hardware/fairphone6)，我們原本設想，這會是朝向一支真正自由、並能作為範例的手機邁進的最佳機會。這麼做是為了掌握哪些 blob 最常見、找出最適合進行逆向工程的 blob，並選出最適合作為初期開發對象的[逆向工程](https://librephone.fsf.org/site/tools/)裝置。不過，我們反而[發現](https://librephone.fsf.org/site/comparing/)了其他狀況：許多我們需要處理的軟體與 blob，其實是多款裝置共用的；這意味著行動電話自由將能取得更大的進展。

即使只是讓手機運算的其中一個面向獲得自由，都是一項龐大的任務；LibrePhone 的工作也會花上很長時間，但在 [1983 年](https://www.gnu.org/)打造一套完全自由的作業系統也是如此。看看 FSF 成立四十年後，我們走到了哪裡！有時候，科技似乎有太多東西都在朝著權力與資本的意志彎折，讓人很難對軟體自由的未來抱持正面想像。我們每天都被各種新聞淹沒：採用 copyleft 授權的軟體正受到[大型語言模型](https://www.fsf.org/news/fsf-is-working-on-freedom-in-machine-learning-applications)威脅、[廠商鎖定](https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026/04/fcc-says-ban-on-foreign-made-routers-includes-portable-wi-fi-hotspots/)日益加劇，以及所謂的「[雲端](https://www.gnu.org/philosophy/who-does-that-server-really-serve.html)」運算。我們也不斷發現新的[授權違規](https://www.fsf.org/blogs/licensing/2026-anthropic-settlement)，或荒謬的[隱私侵害](https://www.fsf.org/blogs/community/2026-ring-offers-mass-surveillance)；而與[科技所有權](https://www.fsf.org/blogs/community/your-digital-life-is-not-yours)及[維修權](https://www.fsf.org/campaigns/fight-to-repair)相關的權利，也需要更堅實的防線。FSF 正努力處理所有這些威脅我們數位權利的面向；但與此同時，我們也說到做到，持續為自由開發軟體。儘管有時看起來難以克服，只要我們成功解放每一個 blob，都是進展。FSF 已經證明...

到了 2026 年，自由軟體運行在支撐網際網路的 [三分之二](https://www.networkworld.com/article/964836/linux-then-and-why-you-should-learn-it-now.html) 伺服器上，在全球前 [500 大超級電腦](https://www.zdnet.com/article/all-500-of-the-worlds-fastest-supercomputers-now-run-linux-exclusive/)中擁有 100% 的市佔率，而[所有程式碼庫中有 98%](https://ia801906.us.archive.org/7/items/rep-ossra-2021/rep-ossra-2021.pdf) 都含有自由軟體。數千萬人也在自己的個人裝置上使用自由軟體，還有數百萬人也可以這麼做。想想這些成功，想想自由軟體支撐全球科技所成就的這些龐大成果，你會發現，我們所倡議的四大自由：執行、修改、複製與分享軟體，早已在日常生活中占有一席之地。我們能夠一起做到的事，經常被嚴重低估，或被那些害怕這些可能性的人阻撓。

就像 1983 年 GNU 專案啟動時一樣，我們已經踏上一段旅程；我們知道這是極其龐大的工程，但既然如今我們許多運算都在手機上完成，這就是一項必要的計畫。我們所需要的，只是時間、讓我們能持續前進的[資金支持](https://my.fsf.org/donate?mtm_campaign=summer26&mtm_source=bulletinm)、[志工](https://www.fsf.org/volunteer?mtm_campaign=summer26&mtm_source=bulletinm)，以及我們的自由軟體精神。讓我們把事情掌握在自己手中，一次處理一個 blob，守護自由。

*「[FSF 紅色的一般手機](https://static.fsf.org/nosvn/bulletin/2026/summer/generic-mobile-phone-in-fsf-red.png)」© 2026, Free Software Foundation, Inc., 作者 Eko Owen。此圖像採用 [Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) 授權。*

#### 文件操作

- **[分享到社群網路](https://www.fsf.org/share?u=https://www.fsf.org/bulletin/2026/summer/ensuring-freedom-one-blob-at-a-time&t=Ensuring freedom, one blob at a time)**
- [新聞](https://www.fsf.org/static/fsforg/rss/news.xml)
- [活動](https://www.fsf.org/static/fsforg/rss/events.xml)
- [部落格](https://www.fsf.org/static/fsforg/rss/blogs.xml)
- [徵才](https://www.fsf.org/static/fsforg/rss/jobs.xml)
- [GNU](http://www.gnu.org/rss/whatsnew.rss)

到了 2026 年，自由軟體運行在支撐網際網路的 [三分之二](https://www.networkworld.com/article/964836/linux-then-and-why-you-should-learn-it-now.html) 伺服器上，在全球前 [500 大超級電腦](https://www.zdnet.com/article/all-500-of-the-worlds-fastest-supercomputers-now-run-linux-exclusive/)中擁有 100% 的市佔率，而[所有程式碼庫中有 98%](https://ia801906.us.archive.org/7/items/rep-ossra-2021/rep-ossra-2021.pdf) 都含有自由軟體。數千萬人也在自己的個人裝置上使用自由軟體，還有數百萬人也可以這麼做。想想這些成功，想想自由軟體支撐全球科技所成就的這些龐大成果，你會發現，我們所倡議的四大自由：執行、修改、複製與分享軟體，早已在日常生活中占有一席之地。我們能夠一起做到的事，經常被嚴重低估，或被那些害怕這些可能性的人阻撓。

就像 1983 年 GNU 專案啟動時一樣，我們已經踏上一段旅程；我們知道這是極其龐大的工程，但既然如今我們許多運算都在手機上完成，這就是一項必要的計畫。我們所需要的，只是時間、讓我們能持續前進的[資金支持](https://my.fsf.org/donate?mtm_campaign=summer26&mtm_source=bulletinm)、[志工](https://www.fsf.org/volunteer?mtm_campaign=summer26&mtm_source=bulletinm)，以及我們的自由軟體精神。讓我們把事情掌握在自己手中，一次處理一個 blob，守護自由。
